title: Support Complementarity
body_html:
Support Complementarity

Let $x \in X(A)$ and $y \in Y(A)$. If $i \in \operatorname{supp}(x)$, then the pure row $i$ obtains the value against $y$. If $j \in \operatorname{supp}(y)$, then the mixed strategy $x$ obtains the value against the pure column $j$.
proof_html:
Let $v=\operatorname{val}(A)$. Since $y$ is optimal for player II, each pure row payoff satisfies $e_iAy\le v$. Since $x$ is optimal for player I, the average of these row payoffs under $x$ is $$ xAy=\sum_i x_i(e_iAy)=v. $$ An average of numbers all bounded above by $v$ can equal $v$ only if every term with positive weight is equal to $v$. Hence $e_iAy=v$ for $i\in\operatorname{supp}(x)$. The column statement is dual: optimality of $x$ gives $xAe_j\ge v$ for every $j$, while optimality of $y$ gives $$ xAy=\sum_j y_j(xAe_j)=v. $$ Thus every positively weighted column in $y$ satisfies $xAe_j=v$.

The Lean formalisation provides separate theorems for the two directions: MatrixGame.support_complementarity_row (rows in $\operatorname{supp}(x)$ hit the value) and MatrixGame.support_complementarity_column (columns in $\operatorname{supp}(y)$ hit the value).

References

  • [MFoGT, Prop. 2.4.1(b)] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory. Complementarity on supports of optimal strategies.

lean_refs.name: MatrixGame.support_complementarity_row
lean_refs.signature:
theorem support_complementarity_row [DecidableEq I]
    (xx : stdSimplex ℝ I) (yy : stdSimplex ℝ J)
    (hxx : xx ∈ A.optimalRowStrategies) (hyy : yy ∈ A.optimalColumnStrategies)
    {i : I} (hi : 0 < xx.val i) :
    A.Ei i yy = A.value

lean_refs.name: MatrixGame.support_complementarity_column
lean_refs.signature:
theorem support_complementarity_column [DecidableEq J]
    (xx : stdSimplex ℝ I) (yy : stdSimplex ℝ J)
    (hxx : xx ∈ A.optimalRowStrategies) (hyy : yy ∈ A.optimalColumnStrategies)
    {j : J} (hj : 0 < yy.val j) :
    A.Ej xx j = A.value
